interpretation: Two training runs with identical seed=42, identical code/config/data, and identical starting checkpoint produced measurably different final checkpoints (43% task-level disagreement, suite deltas up to 20pp, task deltas up to 40pp). This is a training-side effect, not evaluation noise (a same-checkpoint eval repeat of exp0003 was previously shown to be bit-identical on all 21 tasks). Likely cause: no explicit determinism flags are set for multi-GPU DeepSpeed ZeRO-1 training (NCCL reduction ordering, cuDNN kernel selection, dataloader worker scheduling all non-deterministic by default even with seed=42 fixed). This noise floor is comparable to or larger than the effect sizes the 0003->0004->0005 weight-tuning series was trying to attribute to specific design changes, so those results should be treated as unconfirmed rather than trusted or refuted. One exception: libero_goal task 0 reproduced identically (0/5 both runs) -- a genuine, stable, non-noise failure, consistent with a separately-documented interference hypothesis (LIBERO-90's oversampled top/bottom-drawer tasks colliding with this task's rarer 'middle drawer' instruction).

interpretation: Four consecutive generic continued-training extensions (exp0009->0010->0013->0014) each produced large LIBERO-90 gains; this fifth extension (exp0015) produced no material further gain (91.09%->91.78%, within noise) and mild noise-level dips on Goal/Long. Under the project's updated >=95%-on-all-suites goal, this motivates a different next lever rather than a sixth extension of the same kind. Investigated the data mix: LIBERO-90 already contributes ~44% of the training mix by raw episode count even at 1x listing (3921 episodes vs 1940-2165 for the 5x-oversampled Goal/Long), so naive further suite-level LIBERO-90 oversampling is not clearly the right lever and risks diluting Goal/Long. No task-level oversampling mechanism exists in the current data pipeline (RobotVideoDataset/dataset_dirs is a flat list of whole-suite directories). Chosen next candidate: an LR warm-restart (fresh weights-only resume from exp0014 at a renewed peak LR) to test whether the plateau is a shallow-schedule artifact rather than a true limit, before investing in the higher-effort task-level data-engineering intervention.
